questions.subject: PHYSICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: Hydrogen at 324 K emits light ending at n = 1 from n = 4. What wavelength in nm is emitted?

options.misconception: reverses the Rydberg difference giving negative wavelength
uses the wavenumber instead of its reciprocal
converts to metres but labels the answer nanometres

questions.explanation: The Rydberg formula gives one over wavelength as R_H times (1/n_final squared minus 1/n_initial squared); taking the reciprocal and converting metres to nanometres yields the emitted photon wavelength.
questions.hint: Use 1/lambda = R_H (1/n1^2 - 1/n2^2).

questions.stem: Determine the energy in eV of a photon of wavelength 715 nm?

multiplies instead of dividing by the wavelength

questions.explanation: Photon energy is hc over lambda; the convenient form 1240 electron volts times nanometres divided by the wavelength in nanometres gives eV directly, and shorter wavelengths carry more energy.
questions.hint: Use E(eV) = 1240 / lambda(nm).

questions.explanation: Harmonic-oscillator levels are E_v = (v plus one half) h nu; the one-half term is the zero-point energy that remains even at v = zero, so the energy is never zero.

questions.explanation: The photoelectric equation gives maximum kinetic energy as photon energy minus the work function; the work function is the minimum energy needed to free an electron, so it is subtracted from the incoming photon energy.

questions.explanation: The ideal gas law PV = nRT rearranges to P = nRT/V; with R in L atm per mol K the pressure scales with moles and temperature and falls as volume grows, giving the stated value.

omits the molar mass from the density formula

questions.explanation: The two-point Arrhenius form ln(k2/k1) = minus Ea over R times (1/T2 minus 1/T1); solving gives Ea, and the natural log of the rate ratio must be used with the correct sign.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a rate constant from Arrhenius parameters
questions.stem: With A = 4.0e+13 s^-1 and Ea = 62 kJ/mol, what is k in s^-1 at 403 K?

uses a positive exponent giving a huge rate
omits the gas constant from the exponent

questions.explanation: The Arrhenius equation k = A exp(-Ea/RT) gives the rate constant; a larger activation energy or lower temperature makes the negative exponent more severe and slows the reaction.
questions.hint: Compute A times exp(-Ea/(RT)).

questions.subject: PHYSICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: A first-order reaction has k = 0.4543 s^-1. What is its half-life in seconds?

multiplies by ln 2 instead of dividing
uses twice the time constant as the half-life

questions.explanation: For a first-order process the half-life is ln 2 over k; it is independent of concentration, which is why the same expression applies at every starting amount.
questions.hint: Use t one-half = ln 2 / k for first order.

inverts the second-order half-life expression
omits the initial concentration for a second-order reaction

questions.explanation: A second-order half-life is 1/(k times the initial concentration); unlike first order it depends on the starting amount, doubling the concentration halves the half-life.

uses a linear difference instead of the logarithm
uses log base ten instead of natural log

multiplies by n instead of dividing
uses natural log instead of base ten

questions.explanation: The Nernst equation at 298 K is E = E standard minus (0.05916/n) log Q; the cell potential falls as products accumulate because a larger reaction quotient reduces the driving force.

questions.stem: A cathode has E = 0.232 V and an anode has E = -0.16 V as reduction potentials. What is E cell in volts?

options.misconception: adds the two reduction potentials
averages instead of subtracting the potentials
subtracts cathode from anode in reverse order

questions.explanation: The standard cell potential is the cathode reduction potential minus the anode reduction potential; subtraction is used because the anode reaction is an oxidation, the reverse of its listed reduction.

uses the wrong sign for the free energy

questions.stem: Passing 16 A for 8 min deposits a metal of molar mass 87 g/mol with n = 2. What mass in grams is deposited?

multiplies by n instead of dividing
uses minutes instead of seconds for the time

questions.explanation: Faraday's law gives mass = I t M over (n F); current times time in seconds is charge in coulombs, and dividing by n F converts charge to moles of metal before multiplying by molar mass.

divides by n instead of multiplying
reports log K rather than K itself

questions.explanation: Combining delta G standard = minus n F E standard with delta G standard = minus R T ln K gives log K = n E standard over 0.05916 at 298 K, so a positive potential implies a large K.

uses L to the first power instead of L squared
uses twice the particle-in-a-box ground energy

questions.explanation: The particle-in-a-box levels are E_n = n squared h squared over 8mL squared; energy grows with the square of the quantum number and shrinks with the square of the box length, so doubling L quarters the energy.

questions.subject: PHYSICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: An electron box of length 1.74 nm has a transition from n = 1 to n = 2. What wavelength in nm is absorbed?

converts to metres but labels the answer nanometres
inverts the wavelength relation

questions.explanation: The absorbed photon energy equals the level gap delta E = (n2 squared minus n1 squared) h squared over 8mL squared, and the wavelength is hc over that gap with metres converted to nanometres.

questions.stem: An electron moving at 8.10e+6 m/s has what de Broglie wavelength in pm?

converts to nanometres but labels the answer picometres
multiplies by mass instead of dividing

questions.explanation: The de Broglie wavelength is h over momentum mv; faster or heavier particles have shorter wavelengths, and converting metres to picometres requires multiplying by ten to the twelve.
questions.hint: Compute lambda = h/(m v) with m the electron mass.

multiplies by n squared instead of dividing
uses the wrong sign for a bound level

questions.explanation: Hydrogen levels follow E_n = minus 13.6 eV divided by n squared; the negative sign denotes a bound state and the energy approaches zero as n grows, matching the ionization limit. Temperature does not shift the bound levels.

questions.stem: Hydrogen at 244 K emits light ending at n = 2 from n = 3. What wavelength in nm is emitted?

reverses the Rydberg difference giving negative wavelength
uses the wavenumber instead of its reciprocal

questions.explanation: The Rydberg formula gives one over wavelength as R_H times (1/n_final squared minus 1/n_initial squared); taking the reciprocal and converting metres to nanometres yields the emitted photon wavelength.

converts to joules but labels the answer eV

questions.explanation: Photon energy is hc over lambda; the convenient form 1240 electron volts times nanometres divided by the wavelength in nanometres gives eV directly, and shorter wavelengths carry more energy.

reports joules but labels the answer eV
adds a full quantum instead of one half

questions.explanation: Harmonic-oscillator levels are E_v = (v plus one half) h nu; the one-half term is the zero-point energy that remains even at v = zero, so the energy is never zero.

reverses the photoelectric energy balance
adds the work function instead of subtracting it

questions.explanation: The photoelectric equation gives maximum kinetic energy as photon energy minus the work function; the work function is the minimum energy needed to free an electron, so it is subtracted from the incoming photon energy.

questions.stem: A particle is localized to 0.4163 nm. Calculate the minimum momentum uncertainty in kg m/s?

multiplies by the position uncertainty instead of dividing
uses Planck's constant instead of reduced Planck's constant

questions.explanation: The Heisenberg bound is delta x delta p at least h bar over two; a tighter position localization forces a larger momentum spread, and the reduced Planck constant sets the scale.

questions.stem: At 284 K, two states differ by 0.354 eV. What is the upper-to-lower population ratio?

options.misconception: gives the exponent without exponentiating
multiplies by kT instead of dividing
uses a positive exponent for the upper level

questions.explanation: The Boltzmann factor gives N_upper over N_lower = exp(-delta E/kT); the energy gap must be in joules to match k in J per kelvin, and a larger gap or lower temperature depopulates the upper state.

uses log base ten instead of the natural log
multiplies by W instead of taking its logarithm

questions.explanation: Boltzmann's formula S = k ln W connects multiplicity to entropy; the natural log of ten to the k is k times ln ten, and multiplying by k gives the entropy in joules per kelvin.

questions.stem: A molecule with 5 quadratic degrees of freedom at 515 K has what molar internal energy in J/mol?

ignores how many degrees of freedom contribute
uses per-molecule k instead of the molar gas constant

questions.explanation: The equipartition theorem assigns one half R T of molar energy per quadratic degree of freedom, so with f degrees the molar internal energy is f over two times R T.

questions.stem: With molar absorptivity 14072, concentration 1.8e-4 M, and path length 4.38 cm, what is the absorbance?

questions.stem: A bond of force constant 487 N/m and reduced mass 12.33 amu vibrates at what frequency in THz?

questions.subject: PHYSICAL_CHEMISTRY

ignores the number of moles in the heat calculation

questions.explanation: Heat at constant conditions is q = n C delta T; the temperature change, not the absolute temperature, drives the required heat, and the amount of substance scales it linearly.
questions.hint: Multiply n by molar heat capacity by the temperature change.

adds all formation enthalpies without subtracting
subtracts products from reactants in reverse order

questions.explanation: Hess's law gives delta H_reaction as the sum of product formation enthalpies minus the sum of reactant formation enthalpies; the pathway is irrelevant because enthalpy is a state function.

reverses the volume ratio giving negative entropy
ignores the number of moles in the entropy change

questions.explanation: For isothermal expansion of an ideal gas delta S = nR ln(V2/V1); entropy rises when the gas occupies more volume because there are more accessible microstates.

multiplies enthalpy by temperature instead of dividing

questions.explanation: At a reversible phase transition delta S = delta H/T; the enthalpy must be in joules to yield J per kelvin, and the transition temperature is in kelvin.

questions.practice: Apply delta G = delta H - T delta S
questions.stem: At 381 K, with delta H = 92.9 kJ and delta S = 145 J/K, what is delta G in kJ?

options.misconception: divides temperature by entropy instead of multiplying
forgets to convert entropy joules into kilojoules
adds the entropy term instead of subtracting it

questions.explanation: Gibbs free energy is delta G = delta H minus T delta S; because delta S is given in joules it must be converted to kilojoules before subtracting, and a negative result signals spontaneity.
questions.hint: Convert delta S to kJ/K, then compute delta H minus T delta S.

inverts the enthalpy over entropy ratio
applies a spurious thousandfold factor

questions.explanation: The crossover where delta G equals zero occurs at T = delta H/delta S; enthalpy in joules divided by entropy in J per kelvin gives the temperature where the sign of delta G flips.

uses the wrong sign on the exponent

questions.learningObjective: Predict reaction direction from Q and K
questions.stem: For a reaction with Q = 17.67 and K = 5.39, which statement about the net direction is correct?

The value of K changes to match Q

options.misconception: assumes Q never influences the reaction direction

options.text: A larger Q always drives the reaction forward
options.misconception: confuses a large reaction quotient with forward drive

questions.explanation: Comparing Q with K sets the direction: Q below K drives the reaction forward, Q above K drives it in reverse, and equality means equilibrium, because the system shifts until Q equals K.

solves for the remaining reactant instead of the product
